result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain the proximity problem clearly and propose the same fieldset and field markup, with a tight, medium and loose spacing hierarchy. A's values are cleaner and rounder (4/16/32 from a stated scale, set with parent-owned gap). B uses less round numbers like 6, 36 and 10, and spends some space on general control styling. A's claim that the button is over 44px tall is borderline, but this doesn't outweigh its tighter system. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain the proximity problem well and give similar fieldset and div markup. B lays the spacing out as an explicit 4/8/16/32 scale and uses parent-owned gaps, which is a cleaner fix. A's values are less tidy (6, 36, 10) and it adds some control styling that isn't needed. One weakness in B is that the button only gets the same 32px as the gap between groups, though B still calls out that it needs separation.
